content.comment_body: I'm using a [product_name] module ([article_no]) together with [product_name] software [version_no] on a MacBook Pro running macOS 10.11.1 (El Capitan). I installed the latest USB driver from SiLabs (CP210x Macintosh OS X VCP Driver v4) intended for OS X 10.10. I confirmed that the necessary system folders are both present and have proper read/write permissions for all users. When I connect the USB cable and attempt to transfer a program from the software to the hardware module, the computer detects the USB UART and prompts me to choose between '/dev/tty.SiLab_USBtoUART' or '/dev/cu.SiLab_USBtoUART'. However, selecting either results in a communication failure—sometimes no response or an error stating 'Unable to access IP address /dev/tty.SiLAB_USBtoUART' or 'Unable to access IP address /dev/cu.SiLAB_USBtoUART'. CPU usage spikes to about 50% and can only be resolved by rebooting. Has anyone managed to connect a [product_name] device via USB on Mac OS X 10.10 or El Capitan? I'd appreciate any guidance. Thanks for any support.
You can submit a Support Request—this is available for free one time. Then [company_name] will reach out to you.

I've done that, and here's the response I received: 'Hello [user_name], unfortunately I haven't managed to resolve this. The product notes mention requirement for Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard, Lion, Mountain Lion, or Mavericks.' I'm still hoping for further advice from this forum.
That's unfortunate news. Hopefully someone in the forum can help you further.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is facing difficulties establishing USB communication between [product_name] hardware and [product_name] software on macOS El Capitan (10.11.1). Although the system identifies the USB UART, attempts to transfer data fail, resulting in device selection prompts that end in errors and increased CPU usage, necessitating a reboot. Software compatibility appears limited to older macOS versions, leading to continued frustration for the user.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects smooth USB communication between the software and hardware when running on macOS El Capitan, without encountering frequent system errors, reboots, or compatibility issues.
